correctness.rationale: The frozen opening specified oriented nearest-neighbor clocks, whereas its assumptions and proof used one clock per unordered bond. If both orientations have unit rate, the mean starts as 4t rather than the printed 2t, so the distinction changes finite-time formulas. The complete replacement fixes one clock per unordered bond, explicitly gives p=1−exp(−2t) for the two-direction convention, and leaves the polynomial laws intact. On the repaired model, site coverage is decided by the first incident arrival and K_i depends only on four clocks. Writing A=R−M for an arrived clock minus a thresholded local maximum gives a=p−p³/3; adjacent maxima are disjoint, and the shared-neighbor joint maximum probability at distance two is the integral of x y min(x,y) over the square [0,p]². Twice the integral of x²y over 0≤x≤y≤p gives 2p⁵/15. Thus edge covariances at lags 0,1,2 are a(1−a), −p³(p³−6p+6)/9, p⁵(6−5p)/45, yielding the four site polynomials by K_i=A_{i−1}+A_i. The Bernstein certificates give the three claimed strict inequalities for the factored polynomials and hence the covariance signs and V>0. Three sites discarded between blocks of length floor(n^(1/3)) make the main sums independent; their variance is nV+o(n), their normalized sizes vanish, and the bounded-degree covariance of discarded sites gives variance o(n). The same argument applies at saturation. The frozen rational order enumerator was inspected, not executed, and remains applicable to the repaired formulas.
